## a0abd95c485b

**Suspected shortcut reproduced; target unchanged.** Canonical and default generated inputs place at most one horizontal `44` pair per row, so a rival can decorate only the first such pair in each row and still fit that support. The exact validator-lawful counterexample contains two separated `44` pairs in row 1 and one pair in row 3; `self_check` returned no errors at generator SHA-256 `3f58c4ee94a18d112f02095aa2d12c6397b5009ba477c86b20dcde4c4bb7cee6`.

The rival decorates only the first row-1 pair, producing row 1 `[9,4,4,9,0,4,4,0,0,0]`. Actual Racket rule hash `b5f35645e898` decorates both, producing `[9,4,4,9,9,4,4,9,0,0]`; row 3 agrees. Exact input, validator result, and rival output are in `checks/audit/a0abd95c485b/probe.json`; authoritative output and hashes are in `checks/audit/a0abd95c485b/racket.json`.

This shows a support gap between the validator/rule domain and the default curriculum. I did not modify the audit target.
